sample_unit: LLM-generated questionnaire responses (ChatGPT-4 observations from 120 vignettes, each run thrice)

links.outcome: Change in LLM-generated RAND-36 and EDE-Q scores when vignette gender and sexual orientation were varied
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 RAND-36 mental composite differed by gender (male 12.8 vs female 15.1; 95% CI -6.15 to -0.35; P=.04); no gender or sexual orientation effects on EDE-Q overall score.
links.quote: LLM-generated mental HRQoL estimates for AN and BN case vignettes may be biased by gender, with male cases scoring lower despite no real-world evidence supporting this pattern.

links.outcome: LLM output differences across gender and sexual orientation subgroups in vignettes
links.effect: Gender bias found in ChatGPT-4 RAND-36 mental composite (P=.04); none for sexual orientation (P=.71) or EDE-Q overall score; MentaLLaMA results unreliable.
links.quote: MentaLLaMA did not yield reliable results.

screen.reason: Empirical study testing for algorithmic bias (gender and sexual orientation disparities) in LLM-generated psychiatric ratings using simulated clinical vignettes, but it does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
